changed.what: No reference robot of Appendix G.1 is published as URDF, so the URDF importer had no real parity fixture: the bead now vendors the two URDF sources upstream of the sibling catalogue builders (38-link G1, KUKA iiwa 7) with PROVENANCE.toml or a not-run fetch script, compares them with the builders through the airlock, and feeds NS-07 and N14b-24. It also takes in --fold-fixed (N14b-33's fold) with a hand-computed case, moves N14b-33 and VERBS-design from related to deps (no cycle), adds N37-05 and NS-07 to related, gives the path jail its code (FROB-REF-734) and names what is out of scope bead by bead.

The verb line gains the required --name, matching BD-065 and the registry. Determinism is stated as D0. An include outside the import root is refused with FROB-REF-734. The bead takes the MJCF re-import round trips from N14a-25 (mjcf_roundtrip_quad_a, prop_export_import_meaning_mjcf, quad-a thresholds, closure round trip), because they need this importer and N14a-25 is its dependency.

Fixes a build-order contradiction: the MJCF re-import tests needed BD-066, which depends on this bead. The URDF round trip stays (BD-065 is a dependency). The MJCF writer is now checked by reading its output back with BD-065's XML reader: every written placement, inertial (fullinertia) and geom size must parse back to the model's f64 bit for bit. The MJCF round trip and the MJCF half of the property move to BD-066 and are named in Scope Out. The planted 6-digit control now covers both formats. Determinism is stated as D0.
Steps 1 and 6 now use the registered import form with --name and --key; step 6 had no idempotency key.

The export report has ten reverse classes, not nine (the controller assumption was missing), and a test now catches a mapper that omits it. Adds dep N14-REF, the registry that owns FROB-REF-122, which this bead raises (no cycle).

The bead refused restricted visual assets with FROB-REF-310, which belongs only to the scene pack check (refusal division of N19b-02, N37-18, NEGp1-51). A design export now refuses with 733 (licence set, exit 5) and, from M3, 731 (private, exit 5) at the export door N37-18. At M2 the GLB writer applies the door's rule to each mesh's licence entry (a mesh with no entry counts as unknown) until it is routed through the door. The test is renamed and a never-310 mutant added, the e2e negative step and the references are fixed, and related and plan_refs extended.

The reference-robot list was wrong: Cassie and the iiwa 7 are not M1 MJCF or URDF fixtures, and no reference robot is published as URDF. The URDF rows of GATE-SKEL-01 are now the two URDF sources that BD-065 vendors, measured against BD-067's captures (not run until those exist), with Cassie at M3. The round-trip acceptance is limited to what this script measures; N14a-31's rows are cited.

Corrected the pyramid fact. MuJoCo's edge pyramid (n ± μ·tᵢ) grants μ/√2 along a tangent diagonal; the axis-aligned box grants √2·μ. The negative control now plants both forms and the diagonal row (μ·N within 0.5%) catches each. The e2e import command takes the registered form with --format, --name and --key.

design.import has no output option, so the bead now has one import recipe: import with --name and --key, golden import.fbot = design show --section term, loss report via artifact read. Adds the sibling-catalogue manifest fields that ROBOT-fsim-g1 and ROBOT-iiwa7 use (source.lines, source.builder, parameters_provenance, profile, reduction_reason), allowed only for role sibling-catalogue. Adds the tests and a failing fixture for them.

Step 2 uses the recipe's commands with --name and --key, and adds idempotent replay and the term-bytes check. Step 5 is split: at M1 it asserts the no-authorization flags, the reverse report and a licence entry the join can read; the licence entry on exports and reports needs N37-17/N37-18 (M3), so it is logged not run and run by NEGp1-51. Its 22 dependencies, flagged by the graph check, were checked one by one; all are real (the script runs over the 17 M1 robots and calls frob and the MJCF import directly), so they are kept.
The acceptance commands now carry --name and --key, with an idempotent-replay check and a separate key for the refused call.

Takes over at M3 the assertions that need the licence join and the export door: NEG-16 step 5's licence entry on exports, and ROBOT-barkour's two-licence fixture (a report citing barkour, Apache-2.0 with NOTICE, and go1, BSD-3, carries both entries and notices, and the planted drop of the Apache entry fails). Adds an acceptance line and a unit test.

An imported design declares no contact law, so the first check stops at stage 1 with FROB-REF-121 (stages stop at the first refusal). The demo now shows that refusal and its set-contact-law typed-edit repair before the Estimated check, and applies the same edit before the bad-inertia check so that 104 at stage 2 is reachable. Step f gains --name. g1.urdf is identified as BD-065's vendored G1 URDF. Adds dep BD-110 (design.check, no cycle) and FROB-REF-121 to references.

requests.what: Add oracle captures for the two URDF sources that BD-065 now vendors (38-link Unitree G1 and KUKA iiwa 7 URDFs, from the sibling builders' recorded sources): [[model]] rows g1-urdf and iiwa7-urdf with FK fixtures at 10^4 configurations through the pinned MuJoCo URDF compiler, with static-body fusion off so that every link keeps its frame (FACT to recheck at the pin), conventions in the header. Without them, N14b-24's URDF rows of GATE-SKEL-01 and BD-065's acceptance are not run.

Its e2e note says the import path is not run because design.import (BD-065) depends on this bead. Make that explicit: the --fold-fixed import of the real G1 runs in BD-065 (hand case), ROBOT-g1 (real source) and N14b-24 (fold fixture). Remove any step that exports a generated tree and re-imports it with --fold-fixed, or log it as skip with those owners named.

The design.import row lists as inputs only 'a URDF or MJCF document; --strict'. Add --format (urdf|mjcf|fsim-catalog), the required --name, --expanded-by, --fold-fixed (N14b-33 through BD-065) and --reduced (N14b-34). Add FROB-REF-734 to its refusals (a reference or include that resolves outside the import root, path jail N37-11), as the design.export row already does, and the mass-dropped refusal of N14b-34. Add N14b-33 and N14b-34 under 'Extended by'.

The import path uses 'frob design import --format mjcf assets/robots/cassie/source/<entry> --out assets/robots/cassie/import.fbot --json'. design.import has no --out and requires --name and --key; use NEG-15's import recipe as the other 16 file robots now do: '--format mjcf --name cassie --key asset-cassie-<source hash> --json', with the golden import.fbot taken from design show --section term.

The fsim-catalog import command 'frob design import --format fsim-catalog --builder iiwa7' lacks --name, --key and --json. Use 'frob design import --format fsim-catalog --builder iiwa7 --name iiwa7 --key asset-iiwa7-<sibling commit> --json' (NEG-15's recipe, as ROBOT-fsim-g1 now does).

notes: N14b-34 was reviewed and left as it is: its weights, refusal and profile file are correct. 30 of 31 beads changed. 16 of those changes are the same correctness defect in every file-robot bead: the import command used a --out option that design.import does not have and lacked the required --name and --key. It is fixed once in NEG-15 as the import recipe and applied to each bead. The changes that go deeper are: the URDF importer and gate had no real URDF fixture (no G.1 robot is URDF), so the two URDF sources upstream of the sibling builders are now vendored in BD-065; a build-order contradiction between N14a-25 and BD-066 (MJCF round trips moved to BD-066); FROB-REF-310 misused on design export (N14b-21); NS-07 never reaching the Estimated check because of FROB-REF-121 at stage 1; N18a-20's pyramid fact; ROBOT-fsim-g1's validation (4); and the M1/M3 placement of the licence-join assertions (ROBOT-barkour, NEG-16 to NEGp1-51). New deps added, none creating a cycle (graph_check cycles = 0): BD-065 gets N14b-33 and VERBS-design; N14b-20 gets N14-REF; NS-07 gets BD-110; ROBOT-apollo gets N37-05; ROBOT-barkour gets ROBOT-go1. 'determinism exact' was replaced by D0 in BD-066 and N14a-25 for precision only; VERBS-design defines exact as class D0, so that was not an error. All 31 files parse (front matter, valid one-line JSON lists, known dependency keys, seven sections, three test subsections). The slice is settled apart from the five requests.
